title: Quantum Fisher information of driven-dissipative systems from Keldysh path integrals
authors: Malik Jirasek, Igor Lesanovsky, Viktoria Noel
abstract: Driven-dissipative many-body quantum systems can be exploited in quantum enhanced sensing protocols. Here, non-classical correlations may allow one to reach a measurement precision that surpasses the standard quantum limit. The relevant figure of merit for assessing such quantum advantage is the quantum Fisher information (QFI). In a many-body setting its computation is challenging as it requires knowledge of the full system-environment state. Here we make use of a field-theoretical approach, which is particularly well suited for systems with many degrees of freedom. In particular, we show that the QFI can be linked to a Keldysh path-integral. This route leads to a semiclassical expression of the QFI, which is obtained through a controlled expansion in the so- called quantum fields. We benchmark the framework on three systems of increasing complexity: the driven-dissipative harmonic oscillator, the boundary time crystal - which becomes semiclassical at large system sizes - and a two-dimensional array of collectively emitting atoms. We assess in which parameter regimes the semiclassical description holds and gives access to system sizes beyond the reach of exact methods.
summary: This paper develops a field-theoretical approach using Keldysh path integrals to calculate the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) for sensing in open quantum systems. By employing a semiclassical approximation, the authors derive a tractable formula for the QFI applicable to large, complex models like time crystals and atomic arrays. This provides a crucial tool for assessing quantum advantage in realistic, dissipative quantum devices.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of calculating the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) for quantum enhanced sensing in complex, driven-dissipative many-body quantum systems.
main_result: They derive a tractable, semiclassical expression for the QFI by linking it to a Keldysh path-integral formalism, which is applicable to large systems where exact methods fail.
method: The core methodology involves mapping the QFI calculation onto a Keldysh path integral and then employing a semiclassical approximation by expanding the action and evaluating the QFI via the variance of the classical action.
model_or_system: The study benchmarks its method on three systems: a driven-dissipative harmonic oscillator, a boundary time crystal (BTC), and a two-dimensional array of collectively emitting atoms.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), $I_\vartheta$; the semiclassical QFI, $I_{	ext{sc},\vartheta}$; and the system's occupation number $n(t)$ for the oscillator.
important_parameters: Pumping rates ($\gamma_\uparrow/\gamma_\downarrow$), driving strengths ($\Omega$), system size ($N$), and the ratio of driving to decay rates ($\Omega/\Gamma_0$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is the validity of the semiclassical approximation, which involves truncating the action expansion and is known to fail for weak driving in the atomic array case.
figures_summary: Figures compare the semiclassical versus exact QFI rates for the harmonic oscillator, BTC, and 2D atomic array, demonstrating agreement under certain parameter regimes.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the QFI for open systems, develops the Keldysh path-integral formulation, derives the semiclassical approximation, and then applies this framework to benchmark calculations on the harmonic oscillator, BTC, and 2D atomic array.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, scalable theoretical tool (the semiclassical Keldysh path integral) to quantify quantum sensing advantages in realistic, open quantum systems relevant to AMO physics and quantum optics.
